content: 1. Rash occurs in approximately 4% of cases. 2. Blood and lymphatic system disorders include reversible neutropenia (leukopenia) and reversible thrombocytopenia. 3. Cardiac disorders may present as flattening of the T-wave on an electrocardiogram. 4. Gastrointestinal disorders include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, constipation, anorexia, metallic taste, furry tongue, glossitis, stomatitis, and Candida overgrowth. 5. Hypersensitivity and immune system disorders may manifest as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP), urticaria, erythematous rash, flushing, nasal congestion, dryness of the mouth (or vagina or vulva), and fever. 6. Metabolism and nutrition disorders include pancreatitis. 7. Nervous system disorders may include convulsive seizures, encephalopathy, aseptic meningitis, optic and peripheral neuropathy, headache, syncope, dizziness, vertigo, incoordination, ataxia, confusion, dysarthria, irritability, depression, weakness, insomnia, tinnitus, hearing impairment, and hearing loss. 8. Dermatologic disorders include erythematous rash and pruritus. 9. Renal and urinary disorders may present as dysuria, cystitis, polyuria, incontinence, darkened urine, and a sense of pelvic pressure. 10. Other conditions include dyspareunia, decreased libido, proctitis, and joint pain. 11. Blood and lymphatic system disorders may also include hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, thrombocytopenic purpura, neutropenia, and eosinophilia. 12. Gastrointestinal disorders may also include black hairy tongue, dysphagia, enterocolitis, inflammatory lesions (with Candida overgrowth) in the anogenital region, esophagitis, and esophageal ulceration. 13. Nervous system disorders may also include intracranial hypertension, including pseudotumor cerebri, tinnitus, and myasthenic syndrome. 14. Renal and urinary disorders may include increased blood urea nitrogen (BUN). 15. Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders may include maculopapular and erythematous rashes, onycholysis, nail discoloration, exfoliative dermatitis, and photosensitivity. 16. Liver-related conditions include hepatotoxicity and liver failure. 17. Hypersensitivity reactions may include urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis, Henoch-Schönlein purpura, pericarditis, exacerbation of systemic lupus erythematosus, and serum sickness-like reactions. 18. Metronidazole has been shown to be carcinogenic in mice and rats, with tumors affecting the liver, lungs, mammary glands, and lymphatic tissues. It is unknown whether metronidazole is carcinogenic in humans. 19. Hypersensitivity to bismuth subcitrate potassium, metronidazole, other nitroimidazole derivatives, or tetracycline is a contraindication. 20. Co-administration of methoxyflurane with tetracycline has been associated with reports of fatal renal toxicity. 21. Concurrent use of metronidazole and disulfiram within the previous two weeks may result in psychotic reactions. 22. Alcohol or propylene glycol-containing products should be avoided for at least three days after discontinuing metronidazole-containing products, as a disulfiram-like reaction may occur. 23. Severe renal impairment may result in increased BUN levels with tetracycline use, potentially leading to azotemia, hyperphosphatemia, and acidosis. 24. Patients with Cockayne syndrome have reported cases of severe hepatotoxicity or acute hepatic failure, including fatal outcomes, with rapid onset after initiating metronidazole therapy. 25. Prescribing therapy in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection is unlikely to benefit the patient and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. 26. Metronidazole may interfere with certain serum chemistry determinations, such as AST, SGOT, ALT, SGPT, LDH, triglycerides, and hexokinase glucose. 27. Bismuth absorbs X-rays and may interfere with diagnostic imaging of the gastrointestinal tract. 28. Treatment of H. pylori infection is contraindicated in pregnant women, as it can be delayed until after pregnancy. 29. Tetracycline use during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy can cause permanent discoloration of the teeth (yellow-gray-brown) and may inhibit bone development in the infant. 30. Administration of oral tetracycline to pregnant rats has resulted in yellow fluorescence in the teeth and bones of newborn animals. 31. Metronidazole use during pregnancy has been associated with certain congenital anomalies. 32. Tetracycline administered during pregnancy at high doses (>2 g IV) has been associated with rare but serious cases of maternal hepatotoxicity, which may result in stillbirth or premature birth due to maternal pathology. 33. Tetracycline and metronidazole are present in human milk at concentrations similar to maternal serum levels. 34. It is unknown whether bismuth subcitrate is present in human milk. 35. The effects of therapy on the breastfed infant or milk production are unknown. 36. Tetracycline binds with calcium in human milk, and data indicate that oral absorption of tetracycline in infants is low due to this calcium binding. 37. Metronidazole transfers to human milk, and infant serum levels can be close to or comparable to therapeutic levels. 38. Due to the potential risk of tumorigenicity shown in animal studies with metronidazole, breastfeeding women should pump and discard human milk during therapy and for two days after therapy ends, feeding the infant stored human milk (collected prior to therapy) or formula. 39. Capsules should be stored at room temperature (20-25°C [68-77°F]). 40. Adequate fluid intake, particularly with the bedtime dose, is recommended to reduce the risk of esophageal irritation and ulceration caused by tetracycline hydrochloride. 41. If a dose is missed, continue the normal dosing schedule without taking double doses. If more than four doses are missed, contact the prescriber. 42. Photosensitivity, manifested as an exaggerated sunburn reaction, has been observed in patients taking tetracycline. 43. Bismuth subcitrate potassium may cause temporary and harmless darkening of the tongue and/or black stools, which generally resolve within several days after treatment is stopped. 44. Therapy should be prescribed with caution in patients with evidence of or a history of blood dyscrasias. 45. Adding plans allows for comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same class. 46. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current formulary information. 47.
